The build process for this repository is pkstack poteto-mode. Work enters through the
`/poteto-mode` router. The router matches a playbook, and the playbook's steps carry the work.
This file is the repository profile. It carries what the plugin cannot know about this repo,
and it is the authority on this repo's own surfaces, constraints, and commands.

The docs are part of the codebase, not optional commentary.

## Read first

Before substantial work:

1. `docs/000-index.md`, then `docs/001-current-state.md`.
2. The relevant PRD in `docs/040-prds/` for feature or product work.
3. The relevant ADRs in `docs/030-decisions/` before changing architecture, dependencies,
   deployment, data model, or security posture.
4. The finding ledger, `docs/070-quality/004-finding-ledger.md`. Its lessons are this repo's
   recorded defect classes, applied at design time and verified at sweep time. It starts empty
   and grows only from this repo's own findings. Its header carries the mechanism. While it is
   empty or young, the sweep's executors hunt from their own plan over the diff, and the ledger
   fills from what lands.

## Build principles

<!-- Any plugin-owned section, this one included, may be RELOCATED to a repo doc — the heading
     stays here and its body becomes exactly one line, nothing else under it: `Lives in
     `<path>`; that file carries the current text.` -->

- Validate, do not assume. Check assumptions against the code, the data, or the source
  documents before acting on them.
- Ensure full context before changing behaviour. Ask targeted questions only when local context
  cannot answer them.
- Prefer simple, efficient, architecturally clean solutions. Do not optimise for cleverness or
  breadth.
- Preserve valuable project context. If docs move, leave an index or archive pointer so future
  readers can trace the decision.

### Core doctrine

Method-level. This repo's earned lessons live in the finding ledger.

- **A fact introduced at a boundary is REQUIRED at that boundary.** Where absence is a genuine
  domain state, it is a NAMED VARIANT (`carried | none | unavailable`), never `undefined`.
  "Optional so existing callers or fixtures still compile" is not a reason. The churn is the
  diagnostic, and it is paid in the same commit. When requiredness hurts, that is the signal to
  read, not the cost to avoid. Follow the pressure to its source before reaching for `?:`.
- **Requiredness is a property of the fact's JOURNEY, not of a field.** A fact is required at
  every boundary between where it is established and every consumer that must act on it. The
  test is "which consumer can still be REACHED without it?", never "which layer has it?". A
  discriminant is derived from the STRUCTURE that produced the object, never from observing a
  value. A proof returns the POSITIVE fact it proved, never `boolean`. State an invariant
  against the consumer that FAILS, not the layer that is convenient to change.
- **Never branch on a negative under a fail-closed authorization layer. Carry the positive
  fact.** Fail-closed access control makes every negative read ambiguous by design (zero rows
  means both *does not exist* and *not yours*), so a negative can never carry meaning for an
  internal consumer.
- **Enforcement tiers.** What must hold for EVERY writer holds in the DATABASE (`NOT NULL`,
  `CHECK`, trigger). The type system is ergonomics for the writers the compiler can see. A
  comment is a record, not an enforcement. Guarantees closed structurally hold under re-attack;
  guarantees closed by convention regenerate as sibling defects.
- **A test that stubs the thing under test is a test of the stub.** Check that the ASSERTION
  reaches the outcome rather than stopping at the seam, and that the FIXTURE can express the
  attack at all.

## Units and the PR

A unit is the work behind one PR. It answers one named goal, and a unit with two goals is two
units. A checkpoint is one commit-sized coherent change. A unit is usually one to five
checkpoints.

The unit's design package is its probe in `docs/050-probes/`. The premortem writes it before
the build. It carries BASE, the failure classes the design is built against, and the ledger
lessons those classes implicate. The delegate brief carries those annotations verbatim, so a
delegate never re-walks the ledger itself.

For every NEW FACT the design introduces, the probe records a **facts-before-verbs** row.
Occurrence or state, writer set, requiredness per boundary, enforcement tier. A tier of
"convention" needs a written reason in the row.

**Registration happens at PR open.** The Opening a PR playbook updates the probe with BASE, the
clusters so far, and a named close trigger. A registered unit that never closes surfaces as an
overdue register at the next close.

The PR's Verification section names the real path and the outcome of each check, not the
command names. Every unit that swept names the ledger walk there too (`ledger: n lessons swept · k
findings · model/fact/guard a/b/c · j fixed now · m notes with named triggers`). Where the close
ran, that section cites the loop-health row.

## Mechanism first, reachability second

**Mechanism first.** Every finding is classified WRONG MODEL, MISSING FACT, or MISSING GUARD
before any remedy is chosen. A WRONG MODEL finding is fixed now by redesign regardless of who can
reach it, because deferring it multiplies through every checkpoint that composes on it; it is
never a note. A MISSING FACT is fixed by carrying the fact at the layer that first has it, never
by a local conditional. A MISSING GUARD is the one mechanism where a local fix is correct.
Answering a missing-fact problem with a guard is the spiral, every time. Guard density is the
leading indicator: a third conditional on one path means redesign the path now.

**Reachability second**, and only for MISSING GUARD and MISSING FACT. The `reachable` value is one
of `real user today`, `crafted client`, `raw writer`, `operator`, `not today`. It is evidence, not
an opinion, carried at rung 4 or higher of the evidence ladder in the **blast-radius** skill. Rung
4 is running it against the real code; rung 5 is reproducing it in the running app. Below rung 4
the reachability is unproven, and the row says so. The value decides whether the fix lands in this
unit or becomes a NOTE with a named trigger.

**The verdict words are PASS, PASS+NOTES, FAIL.** A FAIL is a WRONG MODEL, or a real user reaching
a false statement today, reproduced on the surface. Every NOTE carries a named trigger. **A unit is
done when no FAIL is open.**

**Fixed by class** means the ledger's promotion into structure — a constraint, a compile-forced
table, a lint, a registry walk — never the instance patch.

## Checkpoint review and the PR verifier

A fresh-context non-author review round runs on a **composed-on checkpoint** inside a unit: a
migration, a boundary value type, a served contract, or a state transition a later checkpoint
writes or reads. It is fed the ledger.

**Every PR carries a non-author verifier.** One agent that did not write the code, working in its
own worktree, driving the real surface through the verification skill at the PR head against its
parent, returning `PASS`, `PASS+NOTES` or `FAIL` and posting that verdict on the PR, where it
outlives the chat. It buys the one property the sweep's executors are denied by design,
independence from the build, and it samples what a builder's own falsification structurally
cannot: the assumption the author never knew they were making. It is independence-first: its own
plan first, the ledger and the sweep's review manifest afterwards as a completeness floor.
Delegates never spawn review rounds or verifiers. The driver does.

The unit's loop-health row records `mode: <verifier model id>·fed|blind`, or `mode: self` where a
close ran with no verifier verdict. Every fourth verifier runs **ledger-blind** as the anchoring
control. The driver counts the rows in the ledger's loop-health table to know when one is due.
No script schedules it.

## The close

`/close-unit` runs **after the PR's verifier posts its verdict and before the owner merges**, on
any unit whose sweep or verifier landed findings. Its promotions land as a commit on the PR
branch.

Triage first, and triage by mechanism, per the section above. Record the judgement either way,
including "patched deliberately, here is why".

The close then looks each cluster up in the ledger and takes the fork. *Covered but unenforced*
promotes the medium. *Not covered* weakens the statement and re-walks sufficiency. A cluster no
lesson claims mints one. The run is recorded in the probe; the loop-health row is appended to
the ledger.

The close states the unit's product-health line: **"of N findings, m wrong MODEL (all redesigned),
k fixed now, p notes with named triggers; verdict PASS+NOTES; journeys driven green"**.

**Size law:** lessons and their evidence accrete in the LEDGER, never here. When a lesson is
fully mechanized, its prose in this file is cut to a one-line pointer.

## Consumer verification

The repo's verification skill (`verify-<project>`) is **mandatory for any change to a shipped
surface**. It has two seats in the Feature playbook:

- **Step 1, before design.** Read the touched surfaces' feature files, and take a live look at
  current behaviour where that is genuinely informative. The design starts from how the product
  behaves today, not from memory of it.
- **Step 5, after building.** Run any repo-level smoke first, then drive the unit's changed
  mapped features through the skill on the matching surface. "Inconclusive" or wrong-surface is
  not a pass.

{{UI_VERIFICATION}}

A unit whose close finds the feature map wrong runs the skill's MAINTAIN mode in the same
sitting. A map/product disagreement is a fork, never an edit: a dead recipe on working product
gets the recipe fixed and re-driven; broken product is reported into triage. Tests are the
unit's floor and never the substitute for the drive.

## Tests before implementation

The primary goal of a test is to verify business requirements and observable system behaviour,
not to lock in implementation details.

- Write tests before implementation for bug fixes and new behaviour.
- Each checkpoint's test-first pass INCLUDES the locking test for every ledger lesson the
  probe's class rows implicate, written as a composed behaviour test that pins the lesson's
  guarantee, never a lesson citation. It is a floor added to the class-derived tests, not a
  substitute for them.
- Test behaviour via public APIs where available.
- Avoid tautological tests that only assert calls into specific internals.
- Test the underlying principle, not one edge case or an over-specific scenario.
- Prefer invariants and property-style checks where they fit the domain. For a state machine,
  prefer a randomized model-vs-implementation walk over hand-picked examples.
- Keep the test infrastructure fast, deterministic, and optimised at all times (shared
  factories, minimal containers, seeded RNG, no flaky sleeps or live network).
- Use Given-When-Then structure where it clarifies the scenario.

## Proportionality

Proportionality lives in the size of each step, never in a skipped step. The premortem scales to
a short probe note, and the sweep's fan-out scales to the diff.

**The sweep is never skipped.** On a small unit it may be a driver-level ledger walk, but the
walk itself always runs. The walk is what makes a small unit provably small.

**The verifier runs on every PR.** A unit with a clean sweep and a PASS verdict records no
loop-health row, because it has nothing to distil. A sweep or a verdict that landed findings
closes with its promotions.

## Commits

Commit at each checkpoint and at meaningful sub-steps. The commit is the system of record.

- Work on a branch in a worktree off the default branch. Rebase into small, ordered commits
  before opening the PR. Prefer five narrow PRs to one large one, and stack follow-ups.
- Write professional, descriptive messages. What changed and why, not a changelog of files.
  Reference the checkpoint and any resolved risk IDs.
- Where the policy below names merging as the owner's act, an agent opens the PR and stops.
{{COMMIT_RULES}}

## Documentation discipline

- Update docs in the same change when behaviour, architecture, operations, product scope, or
  quality posture changes.
- Keep `docs/001-current-state.md` accurate. It is the living repo summary.
- Add an ADR for durable decisions that affect structure, dependencies, interfaces, deployment,
  security, public contracts, or non-functional requirements.
- Add or update a PRD before implementing substantial product or feature work.
- Add a probe when evidence is needed before committing to an implementation.
- Back-annotate on supersession. When a probe or decision closes or supersedes an earlier doc's
  status line or pointer, update the earlier doc in the same commit.
- Do not treat archived or deferred docs as current truth unless a current doc explicitly
  reactivates them.
- Plan files from execution tooling are working scratch, never the record. The durable record
  is `docs/`, updated in the same change. Never cite a plan file as status.
- Every leaf Markdown file under `docs/` starts with a three-digit sortable prefix
  (`001-example.md`). Preserve existing numbers. New files take the band's next number.
